summary: The saved XML plus20 original spin/IBZ WFC files supply the source data for a complete electronic k-slot construction without launching QE. They do not yet constitute a decoded/admitted full-grid frame table.

For this diagonal cubic cell, equal72^3 grids, scalar full-complex orbitals and zero saved fractional translations, direct integer PW-row transport is the preferred construction. The source FFT rotation is a convention reference and independent comparison route, not a compulsory production transform for each band.

The most consequential newly resolved convention is XML rotation ordering: read the flat nine numbers with Fortran order. The three printed lines are columns of QE s, not mathematical rows. A transpose error can preserve star membership while corrupting frame/atom/probe transport.

The actual spatial source is PP/src/pw2wannier90.f90:rotate_evc with PW/src/ruotaijk.f90. KS_Solvers/DENSE/rotate_wfc_k.f90 performs a band-subspace diagonalization and supplies no star unfolding algorithm.

build_pw_factors already uses k+G and MaterialHamiltonian is already a full-PW action. Reuse its algebra and accepted background, adding a provenance-aware reconstructed-basis entry point instead of replacing H0 or synthesizing XML k records.

The remaining substantial operator work is a non-Gamma q=0 ionic adapter and a genuinely rectangular finite-q source/target action/density bridge with explicit folds and adjoints. Kq alone does not implement either bridge.
Complete electronic k coverage is not complete ionic q curvature or spatial domain dynamics. Keep the full regional goal and its missing material/state/environment inputs explicit.

actual_saved_metadata.antiunitary_resolution: The XML has no per-operation time_reversal attributes. Q04:291-309 explains their omission for noncolin=false,colin_mag=-1; Q05 only assigns t_rev when the attribute exists; Q10:63 initializes the module array to zero. Q09:1399-1400 independently enables scalar k-to-minus-k reduction because magnetic_sym=noncolin AND domag is false and noinv=false. Preserve raw absence separately from the source-supported effective scalar default. This is not a physical spinful time-reversal or Kramers statement. Use the explicitly enumerated unitary spatial operations, including inversion, as the proposed actual-material reconstruction policy; only admit an antiunitary route separately if its scalar-Hamiltonian and state transport assumptions are exercised. Never swap up/down or add a degeneracy multiplier.
actual_saved_metadata.wfc_admission_fields: For each exact up/down file bind header ik,ispin,gamma_only,scalef,ngw,igwx,npol,nbnd,k_cart_bohr_inv,reciprocal_bohr_inv,miller and source digest. Existing R02 accepts the little-endian marker4/int32/logical32/float64/complex128 ABI, full-complex npol=1,scalef=1. All20 actual headers still need decoding under those existing checks. ngw is not row count; igwx is. Match XML physical conversions and the spin-local band slice; do not assume equal up/down Miller order from equal byte counts. Raw MV occupations and eigenvalues remain metadata, not chosen preparation coefficients.

slot_and_phase_plan.slot_identity: Use integer mesh index h=(h1,h2,h3),0<=hi<ni and explicit spin. Q01 orders slot=h3+h2*n3+h1*n2*n3 in zero-based form. Keep the canonical modulo index separately from the folded fractional Bloch vector. Derive folding from QE's NINT convention, including half-grid ties; do not use an unexamined round-to-even function. For this unshifted mesh the printed representatives use the negative half-boundary. Physical k=B*k_fractional, with B the saved physical reciprocal columns.
slot_and_phase_plan.representative_selection: Generate slot metadata from the complete mesh and supplied operations, not by replicating each XML matrix according to its weight. Map each slot to an original spin-local representative. Prefer identity on an original representative and otherwise the first declared XML unitary operation satisfying the exact modulo relation; store the chosen operation and all source identities. A different deterministic choice is a gauge policy, not a new physical mode. Compute actual star memberships and compare their quadrature to the raw XML weights in the future oracle; no membership table is claimed computed here.
slot_and_phase_plan.notation: S_op is QE s parsed with reshape(order='F'); f is the stored fractional translation; c=+1 for unitary and c=-1 for a separately admitted antiunitary image. Define integer g by k_target=c*S_op*k_source+g in crystalline reciprocal coordinates. Miller vectors m are columns, never physical Cartesian momenta.
slot_and_phase_plan.source_envelope_contract: Q02 fixes u_target(x)=exp(-2pi i g.x) times u_source(S_op^T*x-f), with complex conjugation of the pulled-back envelope only for the antiunitary branch, and the final constant exp(-c*2pi i k_source.f). Q03 explicitly uses columns of s_scaled and subtracts ftau. This is the primary convention, not a guessed active/passive transpose.
slot_and_phase_plan.proposed_direct_pw_identity: [INFERENCE; proposed oracle target] For each original source row m, m_target=c*S_op*m-g. Its coefficient is exp[-c*2pi i (m+k_source).f] times C_source(m,:) for c=+1, or the same phase times conjugate(C_source(m,:)) for c=-1. For the actual all-zero f and selected unitary policy, this reduces to an exact integer row transport with unchanged coefficients in inherited row order. The reciprocal-shift phase has not disappeared: it is encoded by the integer -g in the target Miller row. Omitting that shift is a wrong envelope gauge even though f=0.
slot_and_phase_plan.target_row_contract: Retain every original source row. The target PW basis is its explicitly labelled symmetry-derived image, not an asserted native non-IBZ file order. Inherited row order is sufficient and avoids sorting/copying; if a canonical target order is requested, store its explicit source-to-target permutation. Original representative frames keep their original row order. Bind source row count, target row count, target Miller values, k and reciprocal basis in the basis identity. A row-bijection/cutoff/grid-alias oracle must establish that this image is the complete corresponding finite-PW basis; byte availability alone does not establish it. Missing rows may not be filled by reusing Gamma rows or silently pruning.
slot_and_phase_plan.why_direct_transport_here: [INFERENCE; proposed implementation choice] The actual signed-permutation rotations, diagonal cubic metric, equal physical FFT dimensions, zero translations and scalar full-complex orbitals allow direct integer PW transport without interpolation or per-band FFT rotation. Use the source FFT pullback as a comparison implementation, not as an assumed requirement. General noncommensurate geometry/spinors are not licensed by this simplification. Local potential/H0/density actions still use the existing physical FFTs; this recommendation only removes unnecessary FFTs from frame reconstruction.
slot_and_phase_plan.gauge_transport: Do not diagonalize or rephase saved columns during unfolding. With a later declared unitary band gauge U, Psi_target=T(Psi_source)U and the same physical preparation requires D_target=U^dagger D_source U for a unitary T; an admitted antiunitary T requires D_source conjugated before that gauge change. For a general invertible raw-frame change W the proposed covariance law is D'=W^-1 D W^-dagger. Preserve S=Psi^dagger Psi and the R10 metric condition, not a claim that raw saved columns are exactly orthonormal. Gauge/little-group path changes must be tested on the represented density and observables, not on phase-sensitive equality of independently chosen eigenvectors.
slot_and_phase_plan.symmetry_of_preparation: An arbitrary caller-supplied D on a representative is not automatically invariant under its little group. A canonical transported family can be explicitly declared as a preparation policy, but a symmetry-invariant material-state claim additionally requires sewing/path consistency, including degenerate blocks. No populations or D are chosen here. Distinct full-grid k slots are distinct one-particle/CAR modes. Any quasifree/block-independence assumption belongs to the state, not to the XML star weight.
slot_and_phase_plan.atom_and_probe_transport: Q10 constructs irt from S_op^T*x_atom-f. That is the real-space argument/pullback convention, not automatically the forward atom map for an actively transformed probe. Preserve integer lattice-image offsets as well as irt; zero fractional_translation does not imply zero atom-image offset. [INFERENCE] The forward atom map for u(r)->u(S_op^T*r) uses the inverse irt permutation, and directions use the corresponding inverse argument rotation. Prefer recomputing each requested physical atom/direction action on the target frame using original geometry; this avoids relying on a manually rotated H32-x archive. If transporting a finite-q ionic pattern, also transform its q and lattice-image phases under the declared Fourier convention and prove them against literal displaced atomic potentials. No extra atom-q phase is appended by intuition.

Same accepted MaterialReference supplies vrs and Kq. Ionic C(q), preparation and region consumers are separately supplied, not invented by this graph.

minimum_reusable_api.allocation_contract: No full-supercell PW-square Hamiltonian, density, covariance or projector-space block-diagonal D. Reuse one accepted physical background and species tables; stream frames, arbitrary full-PW vector/band blocks and selected probe results. Store small factor/Gram overlaps only when actually needed. Finite-q edges can regenerate/load the second frame sequentially or retain a bounded source/target pair; memory scales with those frames, projector factors and physical-grid blocks, not the square of the complete BvK PW dimension. This is not a claim that unrestricted time evolution has fixed rank.
minimum_reusable_api.compatibility_boundary: R09.gamma_probe_actions/gamma_correlations are explicitly selected-Gamma APIs and R10.ActionFactors expects same-basis shapes. Do not pass a rectangular finite-q action through those validators or simply change its labels. Reuse their sign, raw-factor and normalization conventions in a separately typed directed-edge consumer; migrate callers only after its independent oracle. No current source was edited.

non_gamma_q_zero_actions.H0: Existing R03 already forms p=(B*m+k)^T, evaluates/places NC projectors at that p, and applies p^2+V_local,spin+BDB^dagger to arbitrary full-PW blocks. The new task is the full-grid basis/provenance adapter and coverage, not a new Hamiltonian or a saved-band spectral surrogate. Restore the accepted0025 vrs/K fields through R12; no Native backend call is needed for that restoration.
non_gamma_q_zero_actions.periodic_number_probe: At q=0 a periodic number probe is projected multiplication P_k v(r) P_k in the target's own PW rows. The Bloch phase cancels in same-k multiplication. R09's physical-grid mechanism can be reused at non-Gamma with a correctly bound basis, but its current public Gamma-only scope is not an existing admission of the new consumer. Number versus charge and integrated number versus density must remain separate units.
non_gamma_q_zero_actions.density_and_spatial_gradient: [INFERENCE; proposed bridge] For a same-k dyad |L><R|, form periodic density u_L(r)conj(u_R(r))/Omega using R04 amplitude transforms, then sum the declared dyad coefficients and explicit spin/mode weights. Its density gradient at q=0 uses iG; a gradient of the full Bloch orbital instead uses i(k+G). Do not interchange these two operations. The volume factor is required for density and cancels only in the integrated multiplication-probe matrix element under Omega/Ngrid pairing.
non_gamma_q_zero_actions.ionic_gradient: R06 has p=G, not k+G. For a general-k q=0 ionic direction retain the same local derivative field, but build every placed beta and both nonlocal momentum factors from the actual p=k+G. For complex u, use the complex-linear +i source-bra-side term and -i target-ket-side term; do not conjugate u in apply. This adapter remains new work even though its projector and FFT primitives already exist.
non_gamma_q_zero_actions.kernel: R05.apply_kernel accepts complex up/down envelopes and q_bohr_inv already. R08 keeps the native Coulomb threshold and distinct derivative support, and its final XC action is not simply a saved-density-G projection. Reuse these semantics unchanged. A full-k density construction and its physical trace-dual still need their own bridge oracle.

finite_q_and_adjoint_contract.scope: Genuine finite q means a directed map from the full source PW space at k to the full target PW space at k+q modulo a reciprocal vector, not a diagonal-k copy and not a weighted IBZ matrix.
finite_q_and_adjoint_contract.edge_geometry: Keep q in the same complete BvK mesh and compute target integer index by modular addition. Store ell with k_t=k_s+q+B*ell and the reverse edge. Source/target dimensions and row orders may differ. For a requested q not closing the chosen electronic mesh, report missing compatible k coverage rather than interpolate or call a folded Gamma action.
finite_q_and_adjoint_contract.local_envelope_plan: [INFERENCE; proposed oracle target] Using fractional physical-grid coordinates x, local_apply=F_t{exp(-2pi i ell.x)*v_q(x)*F_s^-1 X}. Here F_s^-1 and F_t use the explicit source and target Miller maps. Literal PW element is v_q[m_t-m_s+ell], with physical-grid alias/support convention stated. The reverse Hilbert adjoint is the adjoint of this entire rectangular map, including conjugate field and reverse fold, not merely conjugation of saved-band overlaps.
finite_q_and_adjoint_contract.density_envelope_plan: [INFERENCE; proposed oracle target] For |L_t><R_s|, delta_n_q(x)=exp(+2pi i ell.x)*u_Lt(x)*conj(u_Rs(x))/Omega before dyad/spin sums. Its physical field carries exp(iq.r). This opposite fold sign is essential to the density/potential pairing. Apply the existing q+G density gradient and Kq to that envelope with the density Miller support, not either WFC row set.
finite_q_and_adjoint_contract.local_ionic_plan: Q12:91-106 and Q14:98-104 give the source-supported envelope coefficients: -i[(q+G).u_a] v_a(|q+G|) exp[-i(q+G).tau_a], summed over atoms in original order, with q/G physical units made explicit. Use the existing NC radial tables only if their range covers every requested |q+G|; R05's present default coverage is for saved |G| and the PW cutoff and must be checked for finite q. No extra exp(+/-iq.tau) multiplies u. Retain the actual NC/no-NLCC scope of the accepted inputs rather than silently adding the source's USPP/NLCC branches.
finite_q_and_adjoint_contract.nonlocal_ionic_plan: [INFERENCE; proposed ordinary-NC adapter] For each atom use B_s=B(p_s,tau_a),B_t=B(p_t,tau_a), shared species D, and p_s=k_s+B*m_s,p_t=k_t+B*m_t. Apply i B_t D B_s^dagger diag(p_s.u_a) X - i diag(p_t.u_a) B_t D B_s^dagger X. This keeps BOTH derivative sides. Q14 forms the source +i momentum overlap; Q13 builds the target -i momentum term. The two placed projectors already carry the physical atomic phase difference. Their cross-k product must not be supplied another guessed q phase. For complex u, adjoint means conjugating the pattern and reversing the directed edge, not replacing the source p with target p in place.
finite_q_and_adjoint_contract.q_minus_q: Bind A_q:k->k+q and its actual A_q^dagger:k+q->k as the -q partner with reciprocal/gauge transport. A real physical displacement/observable imposes the appropriate conjugate-pair relation; it is not physical time reversal. At a self-inverse Gamma/boundary q, represent only the corresponding independent real coordinates after its reciprocal gauge is accounted for. For non-self-inverse q pairs, retain real/imag coordinates for one member, not two independent complex noises. Self-inverse q does not mean every directed k-edge matrix is itself an ordinary same-space Hermitian array.
finite_q_and_adjoint_contract.duals: Maintain two named operations: Hilbert adjoint of each rectangular one-particle action; and transpose under the physical trace-bilinear electron/ion pairing. R04.pair/R08 density_potential_pairing are sesquilinear Omega/Ngrid sums and are not automatically the trace-bilinear dual. At finite q the latter pairs q with -q, preserving conjugation/fold conventions. The independent oracle must compare the complete composed density->Kq->potential action and its bilinear dual.
